unit.sep: Classify exact numbers, operate with rational numbers, model quantities and verify results.
unit.careers: Applications in measurement, stock planning and record keeping; these are illustrative contexts, not qualification advice.
unit.focus: Preserve exact meaning while choosing operations, using calculators and interpreting answers.
unit.phenomenon: Two calculators can show similar decimals even when the exact numbers and intended operations differ.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Number cards, conflicting operation results and fictional volume/credit records.
unit.drivingQuestion: How can we make a numerical decision that remains correct beyond the calculator display? KICD: Why are numbers important?
unit.storylineThread: Classification → exact/approximate → operations → grouping → reciprocals → modelling → critique → independent transfer.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Critical thinking and Problem solving: the learner develops interpretation and inference skills as they classify numbers as either rational or irrational numbers.
Self-efficacy: the learner develops self-awareness as they discuss the use real numbers in real life such as in body temperature and blood pressure.
unit.values:
Responsibility: the learner takes care of a calculator when using it to work out reciprocal of numbers.
Respect: the learner develops humility by taking turns while discussing with peers and working out combined operations.
unit.pcis: Health promotion issues: the learner develops healthy practice skills while discussing use of real numbers in recording body temperature and blood pressure.
unit.content: Operations on rational numbers; Reciprocal of numbers; Application of Integers

assessment.instructions: Lesson 8,40 minutes including 4 minutes procedure and 4 minutes final checking. Work independently using RN8 and a calculator; no teaching cards. Give exact fractions where requested, show intermediate operations and use≈ for approximations. Teacher observes calculator use without providing calculation hints.

sections.title: 1. Classify exact numbers
sections.prompt: Classify all five exact RN8 values as rational or irrational. Give fraction representations for rational values; identify which are integers. Explain why a rounded calculator display does not establish that√3 is rational.
sections.exemplar: Rational:0/1,−7/4,0.272727…=3/11,√25=5/1. Integers 0 and 5. √3 irrational. A finite display represents an approximation rather than the full exact expansion of√3.

sections.title: 2. Combined operations
sections.prompt: Calculate A=5/6−[(1/3)÷(−2)] and B=8÷4×3−(−2)². Show working, justify equal-priority processing and give one independent check.
sections.exemplar: A=5/6−(−1/6)=1. B=(8÷4)×3−4=6−4=2. Multiplication/division are processed left to right at equal priority. A reverse check 1+(−1/6)=5/6 or a correct equivalent check is accepted.

sections.title: 3. Reciprocals and calculator evidence
sections.prompt: Find the exact reciprocal of 2/5 and the reciprocal of√3 in exact form. Use a calculator to approximate the latter to 3 decimal places and record your entry/key sequence. Verify the rational reciprocal by multiplication and explain why 0 has no reciprocal.
sections.exemplar: 5/2=2.5;1/√3=√3/3≈0.577. Entry equivalent to 1÷√(3); actual model sequence can vary. (2/5)×(5/2)=1. Zero times any real number equals 0, never 1. Observe actual calculator use separately from written correctness.

sections.title: 4. Interpret the context
sections.prompt: Use RN8 to find the final liquid volume and signed credit balance. If the final liquid is poured into full 2/5 L portions, how many full portions fit and what volume remains? Show units, state an assumption and explain how exact rational reasoning improves this decision.
sections.exemplar: Volume 5/6−1/4+1/3=11/12 L. Balance−20+65−18=27 KES. (11/12)÷(2/5)=55/24≈2.292 portion-equivalents, so only 2 full portions. Remainder 11/12−4/5=7/60 L. Assume exact stated volumes and no spills. Exact calculation distinguishes a fractional portion-equivalent from the whole-number count of full portions; accept another specific decision/check explanation.

rubric.criterion: Classify exact real numbers and distinguish approximations
rubric.excellent: All classifications, rational representations and integer identifications are correct, with a clear exact/display explanation.
rubric.proficient: Correctly classifies and represents the values, identifies integers and explains the display limit.
rubric.developing: Some correct classifications but a representation or exact/display distinction needs correction.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided examples to apply the rational-number definition.

rubric.criterion: Perform and verify combined rational operations
rubric.excellent: Both exact answers and intermediate operations are correct; clearly explains grouping/priority and gives a valid independent check.
rubric.proficient: Both answers are correct with working, correct priority explanation and a valid check.
rubric.developing: Shows relevant operations but has a sign, grouping or verification error.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided support to choose or execute the requested operations.

rubric.criterion: Use reciprocals and calculators with exact meaning
rubric.excellent: Both exact forms, rounded value, entry record and product/domain explanations are correct; observed device use is accurate.
rubric.proficient: Finds both reciprocals, uses the calculator correctly and explains the product and zero exception.
rubric.developing: Some correct reciprocal work but device use, approximation or domain reasoning needs support.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs a worked example to connect reciprocal with a product of 1.

rubric.criterion: Model and explain a practical rational-number decision
rubric.excellent: All results, full-portion count, remainder and units are correct; explains assumptions and a concrete benefit of exact reasoning.
rubric.proficient: Correctly models the contexts, interprets full portions/remainder and gives a relevant assumption and usefulness reason.
rubric.developing: A sensible model is present but a calculation, unit, whole-portion interpretation or reason is incomplete.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided support to connect the context to rational operations and a decision.
